h.strategy: Aim for hypotheses you believe are about 60-75% likely to hold but that a careful expert would call uncertain: conditional effects rather than main effects. Good sources are diminishing returns (an improving edit helps less when the parent already has a similar strong component), damage concentration (a harmful edit hurts more when the parent has few alternative routes or little spare capacity), and asymmetry (adding a capability and removing it need not have mirror-image effects). Each hypothesis should name the mechanism in one sentence. Avoid claims that are merely definitional or true by construction, and avoid claims that need an unusual sign reversal to be true.

hyps.why: Two strong convs into the output node give diminishing returns for the second.
A strong first hop pays off more when node 1 reaches the output through a capable edge.
The conv route already supplies capacity, making the skip path largely redundant.
Removing a route when alternatives are already gone cuts the output off and concentrates damage.
With fewer alternative routes to the output, removing an edge hurts more.
Node 2 is a dead end when edge 5 is none, so a stronger conv into it adds nothing.
Node 2 already has a strong conv input, so another adds little.
With the direct path gone, the route through node 1 is the main one, so removing it hurts more.
When edge 5 is none, node 2 is disconnected from the output, so removing edge 2 costs almost nothing versus hurting otherwise.
A strong direct conv already supplies most of the gain, giving diminishing returns.
